title: Internal Hom and scalar localization under sequential continuity
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and assume that filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the relative derived tensor product [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex], and ambient derived internal Hom $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_R$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $s$ be a global section of $R$ and put $S=R[1/s]$, the sheafified sectionwise localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], whose underlying $R$-module is the telescope $\varinjlim(R\xrightarrow{s}R\xrightarrow{s}\cdots)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-section-localization]. Let $K\in D(R)$ have the following property: for every sequential diagram $(M_n^\bullet)$ of complexes of $R$-module sheaves with one common termwise lower bound, the evaluation-induced comparison
$$\varinjlim_n H_R(K,M_n^\bullet)\longrightarrow H_R(K,\varinjlim_n M_n^\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism; filtered colimits here are exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial complex representatives [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then for every $L\in D(R)$ whose cohomology vanishes in sufficiently negative degrees the canonical evaluation-transpose map
$$S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\longrightarrow H_S(S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$, natural in $K,L$. Its restriction to $D(R)$, under the evaluation-normalized scalar adjunction, is the sequential-continuity isomorphism $S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\simeq H_R(K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$. No constructibility, completeness, or perfectness hypothesis is imposed beyond the displayed continuity assumption.

proof.text: Choose $a$ with $H^i(L)=0$ for $i<a$ and a representative $M$. Put $P^i=0$ for $i<a$, $P^a=\operatorname{coker}d_M^{a-1}$ and $P^i=M^i$ for $i>a$, with induced differential. The quotient $M\to P$ is a quasi-isomorphism: cohomology agrees in degrees at least $a$, and both vanish below $a$. Hence $(P,s)$ has a common termwise lower bound.

proof.text: Write $F=S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ and $U$ for restriction. The derived-localization reflection lemma identifies them with exact termwise extension $E$ and restriction $U_0$, with unit $\eta:x\mapsto1\otimes x$, and gives the scalar-unit Hom-bijection. Apply the complex-colimit theorem with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z[T]$, $T\mapsto s$: for every complex $B$, its scalar colimit is $U_0E(B)$ with $n$th leg $U(s^{-n})\eta_{QB}$. Exact filtered colimits preserve quasi-isomorphisms, since cohomology is kernel modulo image; these identifications therefore apply to the stipulated representatives, even if $B$ is unbounded.

proof.text: Represent $K$ by $A$ and put $X=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I(P))$, representing $H_R(K,L)$. The K-injective Hom scalar-telescope lemma identifies the colimit of $(X,\mathcal Hom(A,I(s)))$ with that of $(X,s)$, preserving every leg. Compose its inverse with the assumed continuity isomorphism for the bounded-below input tower $(P,s)$ and the two scalar-colimit identifications of step 2. This yields $\beta:UFH_R(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(K,UFL)$ with $\beta\eta_{H_R(K,L)}=H_R(K,\eta_L)$, because continuity is evaluation-induced and all identifications preserve the zeroth leg. No lower bound on $X$ is used.

proof.text: Let $\chi:FH_R(K,L)\to H_S(FK,FL)$ be the stated evaluation-transpose map and $\alpha:UH_S(FK,FL)\cong H_R(K,UFL)$ the scalar-Hom adjunction isomorphism. Their evaluation normalization gives $(\alpha U\chi)\eta=H_R(K,\eta_L)$: both transposes are evaluation followed by $\eta_L$. The target is isomorphic to $UN$ for $N=H_S(FK,FL)$, so scalar-unit uniqueness gives $\alpha U\chi=\beta$. Thus $U\chi$ is invertible, and conservativity of $U$ makes $\chi$ invertible. This also identifies its restriction with sequential continuity. Naturality in $L$ and contravariant naturality in eligible $K$ follow from functorial evaluation, scalar extension, transposition and $\alpha$.
